text:
maria: @channel FYI customer acme-prod reported a 15m window with repeated 429s + 5-12s tail latency during a traffic spike. They’re on Dedicated (pool p-12345, us-west-2). Root says requests queued while new workers were still initializing.
jamal: Can you paste the example request IDs / timestamps? I’ll pull autoscaler logs.
sophie: Monitoring: saw a scale intent at 2025-07-12T14:23:10Z but pool did not reach target until ~14:23:40Z. Convergence ~30s. infra-bot flagged autoscaler_convergence_time high.
maria: Example request IDs: rq_8f3a, rq_8f3b. Customer repro env: burst of ~200 reqs/sec for ~30s. They hit token endpoint and a lot of replies were 429.
kim: Quick sanity: min_instances for that customer is 1, max 20, spawn_concurrency=2, provision_backoff=8s, scale_hysteresis=30s. Also preheat=false on their profile.
jamal: That config combo explains it: when a spike hits from 1->needed 6 instances, autoscaler issues multiple create calls but spawn_concurrency=2 serializes creation, hysteresis prevents aggressive retries. Net effect: slow ramp and request queueing.
infra-bot: Alert: registry_pull_retry_count increased for pool p-12345 between 14:22-14:25 (possible image registry throttling) — see <https://internal.registry/ops/ev/4321>
maria: Customer also mentioned a couple of auth errors earlier, but billing checks show their account in good standing so not a billing block.
sophie: Logs show several nodes stuck in InitContainer due to heavy kubelet CPU (OOM logs on kubelet) and one image pull 429. Combined with spawn_concurrency this amplified delay.
maria: Repro steps I ran locally that reproduce the symptom:
```
ab -n 1000 -c 200 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.test/dedicated/acme-prod/generate
# observe 429 spread and time-to-first-byte jump to >5s
```
jamal: Mitigation plan:
- temporarily bump min_instances -> 3 for acme-prod
- set preheat=true for their profile
- increase spawn_concurrency -> 5 to allow parallel provisioning
- add short-term increase to registry pull parallelism
I can push changes if folks OK.
kim: I’ll open infra ticket and check if registry team saw throttles. If they confirm, request short quota bump for image pulls.
support-ops: Customer agreed to mitigation. Please apply and notify.
jamal: Applying config changes now (patch: set min_instances=3, preheat=true, spawn_concurrency=5). Will monitor for 15m.
infra-bot: Config change rollout started at 2025-07-12T14:40:02Z for pool p-12345.
jamal: Rollout finished 14:40:45Z. Autoscaler metrics show new instances in pool by 14:40:55Z.
maria: Customer reports reduced latency and no new 429s for the last 12m :tada:
sophie: Root cause summary:
- low min_instances (1) + aggressive burst workload
- spawn_concurrency intentionally throttled which serialized provisioning
- an unrelated transient registry throttling event increased individual node init times
- autoscaler hysteresis/backoff settings made the control loop slow to catch the spike
Follow-ups: expose spawn_concurrency + convergence_time in Console; add onboarding recommendation: "burst-prone Dedicated customers should have min_instances >=2 and preheat enabled"; add a playbook for registry throttle detection.
kim: Filed TRACK-1419 for Console metric and SUP-9876 for customer follow-up. Assigned to infra + devex.
support-ops: Thanks team — customer escalated to success; will close once we confirm no recurrence in 24h.
jamal: I’ll draft a short post-incident note and configuration guide for support runbook.
maria: Thanks all. If anyone needs the logs I dropped them to /internal/support/1752109876/logs (internal only).
